hyperparameters.context: Used in the position matrix to represent vehicles in the control area.

nodes_source.source_quote: In this work, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) method to explore the potential of traffic video data in improving the efficiency of ramp metering.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic video data from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices, used as inputs for the deep reinforcement learning method.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle locations from raw traffic video frames.

nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m_t
nodes_process.description: The DRL method uses traffic video frames as input to learn optimal control strategies for ramp metering. Vehicle locations are extracted from raw images and reformed into position matrices. These matrices are then stacked over N consecutive time steps to form the state input for the Q-network. Down-sampling is applied to reduce input dimensions. The Q-network is a deep neural network with convolutional and fully connected layers, extended for multitask learning to predict speed and queue length alongside Q-values. Training uses Adam optimizer, experience replay, and a target network to minimize a combined loss function. The method is evaluated in SUMO against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines, and through a perturbation analysis.

nodes_process.source_quote: The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase in the current signal cycle based on the length of the red phase in the previous cycle and the downstream occupancies in the previous and current cycles.
nodes_process.description: Implement the PI-ALINEA ramp metering method as a baseline. This method fixes the green phase length and determines the red phase length based on previous red phase length and downstream occupancies.
parameters_mentioned: green time for each cycle is fixed with time step size L

nodes_process.source_quote: The results demonstrate that, in comparison with a state-of-the-practice method, the proposed DRL method results in (1) lower travel times in the mainline, (2) shorter vehicle queues at the on-ramp, and (3) higher traffic flows downstream of the merging area.
nodes_process.description: Compare the performance metrics (travel times, queue lengths, traffic flows, speeds) of the DRL method, PI-ALINEA, and no-control scenarios.

nodes_process.source_quote: As shown in Figure 15, the control area is divided into eight subareas. The information in the subarea is removed from original data to generate perturbed data for each subarea.
nodes_process.description: Divide the control area into eight subareas. For each subarea, remove its information from the original data to generate perturbed data.
